footer.pequeno_texto: A fast, online tool for switching between text formats and code naming conventions.

home_text_section.p_sobre: “Cases” are a set of conventions and formatting rules used to combine multiple words into a single identifier without using spaces.

card1.title: Why do they exist?
card1.description: In programming languages, variable, function, and file names cannot contain spaces. Naming conventions were created to keep code readable and standardized.

card2.title: Code vs Web
card2.description: Different contexts call for different styles. While APIs and databases use formats like snake_case, web URLs typically require kebab-case or slugify for SEO-friendliness.

card3.title: Team Standardization
card3.description: Each programming language follows a market standard (e.g., JavaScript prefers camelCase, Python uses snake_case). Adhering to these conventions helps prevent bugs and makes the code easier for the team to read.

sobre.p: Learn about the concept and principles behind the tool.

sobre_text.title: What is CaseFlex?
sobre_text.p1: was created by a solo developer who wanted to hone his skills in Next.js, React, internationalization, and SEO, and to launch projects.
sobre_text.p2: This project is the third one I've created on my own, as part of my effort to become a better developer.

diferenciais.d1: Your text never leaves your browser. It is not sent to external servers.
diferenciais.d2: Using sessionStorage so you don't lose your text when you accidentally switch tabs.
diferenciais.d3: Built with Next.js, React, and Tailwind CSS using a modular architecture.
diferenciais.d4: Designed to speed up the formatting of variables, constants, and slugs for the web.
